wiki-iran.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on Iran each day. It jumps when the country is at the centre of a war, a negotiation or a crisis, so the spikes mark the days the wider world went looking for background.
wiki-iran.recent: Mossad reportedly warned Washington of explosive drones aimed at Trump. In the days after, Iran said mines hit 4 tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and a third US carrier reached the Gulf. Then the US bombed Qeshm Island, and Iran struck Bahrain and an airbase used by US forces in Kuwait.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of North Sea crude, and the reference against which most of the world's internationally traded oil is priced. Petrol, diesel and jet fuel costs follow it, and so do the budgets of oil-exporting states.
brent.recent: The US-Iran war has turned the Strait of Hormuz into a minefield: Iran says mines hit 4 tankers in 24 hours, and a senior US Navy official put the cost of insuring one transit at $64m. Supply is finding other routes. Iraq's Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline pumps crude again after a decade, and Russia's crude shipments hit their highest since late July.

wti.standing: West Texas Intermediate: the price of a barrel of light, sweet crude delivered at Cushing, Oklahoma, and the benchmark for American oil. US petrol and diesel prices follow it, and so do shale drillers' budgets.
wti.recent: Brent fell below $90 for the first time since August after Trump called a new Iran offensive 'highly unlikely', while Russia shipped its most crude since late July and China and India paid a premium for its sanctioned barrels. Mine strikes in the Strait of Hormuz, where Iran says 4 tankers were hit in 24 hours, lifted prices only briefly.

natgas-hh.standing: The futures price of gas delivered at Henry Hub in Louisiana, the benchmark for the American market. It moves on weather, storage and LNG exports, and sets what US power plants and households pay for heat and electricity.
natgas-hh.recent: The gas news was about Hormuz, not US fields: an LNG carrier hit a mine in the strait, the IMF said Qatar's economy would shrink more than 14%, Iran forecast a winter deficit and Pakistan rationed gas. That tightens the seaborne market US exporters sell into, though none of it speaks to US supply or weather.

wheat.standing: The export price of a tonne of US hard red winter wheat loaded at the Gulf of Mexico, a reference for bread wheat worldwide. Importers from Egypt to Indonesia buy against it, and bread subsidy budgets strain when it rises.
wheat.recent: A wheat ship capsized off Bulgaria after a reported sea-drone strike, and hopes that trilateral talks would free up the Black Sea pulled wheat lower in November. Both came after the last monthly reading, and nothing reported explains the earlier peak.

rice.standing: The export price of a tonne of Thai white rice, the benchmark much of Asia's and Africa's import trade is priced against. Rice is the staple for about half the world, so a move here reaches household food budgets directly.
rice.recent: The month's rice news was about growing it: a call for Southeast Asia to breed rice that outlasts El Niño, a new disease discolouring grain in Bangladesh, and a UN plea to let fertilisers through Hormuz. None of it accounts for the export price.

copper.standing: The price of a tonne of refined copper, the metal in every wire, motor and transformer. Demand follows construction and electrification, and supply rests on a handful of mines in Chile, Peru and the Congo.
copper.recent: In London the metal fell to $13,778 a tonne in early November, its lowest since July, on fears about AI. The hunt for new supply went on regardless: Adani agreed to finance Codelco's Kaburkaala exploration in northern Chile, and in Bacolod protesters turned on a proposed copper mine tied to Pax Silica, the US push to secure critical minerals.

us-10y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for ten years, set by trading in its bonds. Mortgages, corporate loans and other governments' debt are priced off it, so it sets the cost of money well beyond America.
us-10y.recent: October's consumer prices rose 0.4%, beating forecasts, and the Fed's Logan called for two more rate hikes, possibly rapidly. Minutes of the October 27-28 meeting then showed almost all officials expected further tightening, and Mary Daly now openly argues for hikes. Lenders asked more to tie up money for ten years once a higher Fed rate looked likely.

sp500.standing: An index of 500 large companies listed on US stock exchanges, weighted by market value. It is the benchmark most pension and index funds are measured against, and a handful of technology firms carry much of its weight.
sp500.recent: The slide began with the chipmakers that had carried it: after the midterms' blue wave and a backlash against data centres, Nvidia fell 6%, AMD 12% and Micron 11% in one session. The selling crossed to Asia the next day, where South Korea halted trading after the Kospi fell 8%.

nasdaq100.standing: The 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange in New York, weighted by size. A handful of technology giants make up most of it, so it reads as the price of American big tech.
nasdaq100.recent: The slide came as chipmakers sold off after the midterms amid a backlash against data centres: Nvidia fell 6%, AMD 12% and Micron 11% on Thursday, and the rout spread to Asia, where the Kospi fell 8%. A week later Nvidia futures fell nearly 12% on reports its board may oust Jensen Huang.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average price US drivers pay for a gallon of regular gasoline at the pump, taxes included. It follows crude oil and refining costs with a lag, and it is the energy price American households and voters notice most.
us-gas-retail.recent: Pump prices followed crude lower as the Iran war's oil shock priced out demand. Ukrainian drones on refineries like Kirishi left Russia with less to refine and more to export, lifting its crude shipments to their highest since late July. The US still raised its forecasts for 2027 gasoline and diesel prices.

natgas-ttf.standing: The wholesale price of natural gas in Europe, set at the Dutch TTF hub where the continent's pipeline and LNG supplies are traded. Household heating bills, power prices and fertiliser costs across the EU follow it.
natgas-ttf.recent: The reporting since the last reading is about supply at risk, not the rise itself: a mine struck a liquefied natural gas carrier in the Strait of Hormuz, a drone attack suspended production at Iraq's Khor Mor gasfield, and Iran forecast a winter gas deficit. All of it came after the reading, so none of it explains the climb.

vix.standing: The CBOE Volatility Index: the swing in the S&P 500 over the next 30 days implied by the prices of its options. It rises when investors pay more for protection against a fall, which is why it is called the fear gauge.
vix.recent: The fortnight's market news centred on Nvidia's leadership crisis after Jensen Huang's exit, which the company answered with a $130 billion fourth-quarter revenue forecast. That came after the peak, and nothing reported in the window explains the climb that preceded it.

fx-pkr.standing: What one US dollar costs in Pakistani rupees, under a float the State Bank of Pakistan manages. Pakistan pays for its fuel imports in dollars, so a weaker rupee reaches pump prices and household bills.
fx-pkr.recent: Pakistan's money news came from lenders and the Gulf war: the Asian Development Bank granted a $500M pension loan, the central bank saw inflation back at 5-7% in the 2027 fiscal year, and the Hormuz closure cut mango export earnings from $100 million to $60 million. None of it accounts for the rate.

fx-ngn.standing: Nigeria's currency, quoted as naira per US dollar. Africa's most populous country earns most of its dollars from crude oil and imports much of what it consumes, so the rate sets what fuel and food cost there.
fx-ngn.recent: The fortnight's Nigerian news centred on oil already spoken for: 340 million barrels of future crude reportedly back 11.2 trillion naira in loans, and Atiku proposed reviewing that crude if elected. None of it was a policy, supply or central-bank event that accounts for the rate.

fx-egp.standing: How many Egyptian pounds buy one US dollar. Egypt imports much of its wheat and fuel and owes heavily in dollars, so a weaker pound feeds straight into food prices and the cost of servicing its debt.
fx-egp.recent: Cairo spent the month hunting for dollars. The Suez Canal earned $724 million in October, roughly double, a decree pledged 112 million square metres of Red Sea coast against public debt, and Aswan's informal miners, once jailed, will now be paid on the spot for their gold. None of it explains the late-October slide itself.

fx-try.standing: How many Turkish lira buy one US dollar, so a rising line is a weakening lira. Turkey imports most of its energy and its companies owe heavily in foreign currency, so the rate feeds straight into prices and repayments.
fx-try.recent: Turkish savers who hold gold as their shield against the lira lost part of that cushion when gold fell 6.4% in 7 days to $3,853 an ounce on 16 November. That hit household balance sheets, but nothing in the fortnight's news accounts for the lira's own slide against the dollar.

fx-bdt.standing: What one US dollar costs in Bangladeshi taka, a rate the central bank manages closely. Garment exports and remittances from workers abroad supply the dollars; fuel, cotton and food imports spend them.
fx-bdt.recent: The news from Dhaka over the window was political: Sheikh Hasina applied for a Bangladeshi passport and identity card, a step toward returning from India. None of it explains the exchange rate.

fx-idr.standing: How many rupiah one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker currency. Indonesia sells coal, nickel and palm oil in dollars and relies on foreign buyers for its bonds, so it moves with commodity prices and capital flows.
fx-idr.recent: The push came from Washington rather than Jakarta: bets on the Fed lifted the dollar and drove the rupiah to a record low. At home, Prabowo was reported to have accepted his vice president's resignation in the same stretch, though nothing in the input ties that to the currency.

fx-lbp.standing: The price of one US dollar in Lebanese pounds. Lebanon imports most of its food, fuel and medicine and pays for them in dollars, so the rate sets what a salary earned in pounds can buy.
fx-lbp.recent: The fortnight's Lebanon news was about the war's aftermath rather than money: the army seized a large weapons depot in Beirut's southern suburbs, and the Bekaa Valley was left with 24% of Lebanon's wheatland fallow. None of it accounts for the pound, which the central bank holds near a fixed rate.

fx-cny.standing: How many Chinese yuan one US dollar buys. The central bank sets a daily reference rate and lets trading stray only 2% either side, so the rate is partly policy, and it decides how cheap Chinese exports are abroad.
fx-cny.recent: China's central bank said nearly 30% of goods trade now settles in yuan, as sanctions on Russia and Iran made dollar payments a risk. HKEX launched an index of 305 offshore yuan bonds, and Citi forecast the yuan at 6.5 per dollar by mid-2027. All three concern the currency's reach abroad, and none explains its drift against the dollar.

fx-inr.standing: How many rupees buy one US dollar, so a rising line is a weakening rupee. The Reserve Bank of India manages it loosely, and because India imports most of its oil, a weaker rupee raises fuel prices for 1.4 billion people.
fx-inr.recent: The rupee's firming came as October exports jumped 30% and the trade deficit narrowed to $20.09 billion, which meant less demand for dollars. The same day, retail inflation reached 6.09%, a two-year high that breached the central bank's ceiling and put a tighter policy on the table.

fx-brl.standing: How many Brazilian reais one US dollar buys; a higher number is a weaker real. Brazil exports soy, iron ore and oil and pays high interest rates, so the currency moves on commodity prices and on doubts about public spending.
fx-brl.recent: Brazil's investor class soured on Lula after his runoff win, and the fiscal gap is the worry behind it. The Senate passed the government's fiscal adjustment bill with 45 votes, and October inflation of 4.63% came in below forecasts, yet neither was enough to win back the money betting against the real.

fx-mxn.standing: The number of Mexican pesos one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker peso. Latin America's most traded currency, it moves on US trade policy and interest rates, because most of Mexico's exports go north.
fx-mxn.recent: Trump threatened to double tariffs on Mexico unless migrant caravans were stopped, after 1,500 migrants set out walking north from Tapachula. Tariffs fall on the exports to the United States that earn Mexico its dollars, so the threat reaches the peso directly.

fx-eur.standing: How many euros one US dollar buys. The euro is shared by most European Union states and is the world's second reserve currency; it moves on the gap between ECB and Federal Reserve interest rates.
fx-eur.recent: The euro's weakening followed France: the European Central Bank said markets, not it, should discipline indebted states, as France's borrowing premium over Germany hit 1.75 points and Ifop polls put Le Pen and Mélenchon ahead of a stalled centre. Washington also sold $500 million of euros to buy yen.

fx-jpy.standing: How many yen one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker yen. Japan pays for nearly all its energy in dollars, and its low interest rates have long made the yen the currency the world borrows cheaply.
fx-jpy.recent: Japan spent a record ¥7.98 trillion in one day buying yen, and Washington then sold $500 million of euros for yen as the rate pressed against the 160 line. The weakness has been a gift to exporters: nearly half of Japan's manufacturers raised profit forecasts on the soft currency.

fx-rub.standing: How many rubles buy one US dollar. Russia earns its foreign currency mostly from oil and gas, and sanctions and capital controls shape the rate, so it moves on energy prices and state policy as much as on trade.
fx-rub.recent: Drone strikes on Russia's refineries left more crude to ship abroad, and exports reached their highest since late July, a flow of dollars that props up the ruble. Against that, the EU sanctioned the Wildberries founder and proposed a €45 billion Ukraine loan tied to Russian reparations. None of it produced a sharp break in the rate.

fx-zar.standing: South Africa's currency, quoted as rand per US dollar, so a rising line means a weaker rand. One of the most traded emerging-market currencies, it moves with the metals the country exports and with global appetite for risk.
fx-zar.recent: The fortnight's South African news was domestic. Left parties holding 20% of the vote set conditions for backing the ANC, and a GDP rebasing that counted illegal miners raised mining output 12.5%. Neither accounts for the rand weakening against the dollar.

btc.standing: The dollar price of one bitcoin, the first and largest cryptocurrency, whose supply is capped at 21 million coins. It trades around the clock, and the rest of the crypto market tends to move with it.
btc.recent: Spot bitcoin ETFs lost a net $1.282 billion in a single week, and $1.3 billion of crypto futures were liquidated in 24 hours as falling prices forced out leveraged bets. MSCI then dropped Strategy, owner of 850,364 bitcoin, from its indexes, putting the treasury-buying model in doubt, while money rotated toward the Anthropic listing.

eth.standing: The token of the Ethereum network, the blockchain most stablecoins, lending protocols and tokenised assets run on. Every transaction there is paid for in it, so its price tracks use of the network as well as appetite for crypto.
eth.recent: Ethereum fell with bitcoin, which dropped below $75,000 and then below $65,000, with miners leading Wall Street's crypto sell-off. Its own news cut the same way: an Ethereum Foundation developer counted up to 15,000 contracts the Glamsterdam upgrade risks breaking, and compatibility problems have stalled testing on the Hoodi testnet.

paxg.standing: The dollar price of a troy ounce of gold on New York's COMEX futures market. Gold pays no interest, so it tends to fall when yields and the dollar rise, and central banks and households buy it when they distrust currencies.
paxg.recent: The slide followed the Fed's turn toward hiking: governor Christopher Waller urged a half-point rise in December, and traders now price one at about 96%. A firmer dollar makes a metal that pays no yield costlier to hold, and the loss lands on households in Turkey, who keep their savings in gold.

wiki-russia.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on Russia each day. It jumps when the country does something the wider world wants explained, so it marks which events reached people who do not follow the news closely.
wiki-russia.recent: A car bomb in Moscow injured Sergei Zavorotny, a former adviser to Mykola Azarov, the second such blast in two days. Days later Ukrainian drones hit the Crimean Bridge at Kerch, and Trump, Xi and Putin met in Shenzhen at a summit where Ukraine, Europe and Japan had no seat.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on the channel between Iran and Oman through which Gulf oil and gas reach the open sea. About a fifth of the world's oil passes through it, and no sea route goes around it.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: Iran says ships off its authorised lanes are hitting mines: 2 supertankers carrying over 4 million barrels, a liquefied natural gas carrier, then 4 tankers in 24 hours. Rezaei says the strait stays shut until Iran's seven conditions are met; Acting US Navy Secretary Hung Cao says one transit costs $64m to insure.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: Mines, not a blockade, are emptying the strait: Iran says mines hit 4 tankers in 24 hours, and Acting US Navy Secretary Hung Cao told senators one transit costs $64m to insure. The trade behind it is paying: the IMF says Qatar's economy will shrink more than 14%, and Pakistan's mango earnings fell from $100 million to $60 million.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: A Japanese container ship transited the strait for the first time in three years on the day Yemeni government forces withdrew from the area, leaving Houthi forces holding the Bab el-Mandeb coast. They have since pressed on Aden, the government's seat, while Saudi-led strikes hit Hodeidah and Houthi missiles reached Riyadh.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: Shipping is coming back to the Red Sea route. The canal earned $724 million in October, double its earlier take, and a Japanese container ship transited Bab al-Mandab for the first time in three years. Days later the Houthis freed 600 fighters as Yemen forces were redeployed, and pressed an advance in Yemen that sits beside the route's southern gate.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.
cp:panama.recent: The stories out of Panama City this fortnight were about Etesa's swollen transmission contracts and the bombing of reporter Rolando Rodríguez's home. Neither touches the canal, and nothing in the news accounts for the traffic.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Ships bound for the strait now sail through a drone campaign at sea. At least 7 Black Sea vessels were reportedly hit in a single month, drones struck 3 ships inside Romanian waters, and a wheat carrier capsized off Bulgaria with all 12 crew saved. Von der Leyen pledged €50 million to speed up an EU security hub for the Black Sea.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: The fortnight carried a Spanish general strike that unions said 90% of port workers joined, Storm Charles shutting schools and grounding flights in Portugal, and an EU boarding of a Russia-linked "shadow fleet" tanker. None of it is tied to traffic through the strait itself.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.
cp:dover.recent: The fortnight's French news was about wage strikes, Yellow Vest protests, the presidential race and a freezer cyberattack that prosecutors blamed on Iran's Revolutionary Guards. None of it touched shipping in the strait or explains the traffic.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: A Japanese container ship transited Bab al-Mandab for the first time in three years, a return to the Red Sea route this detour replaced. One transit does not account for the thinner traffic here, and the mine and projectile strikes on tankers in Hormuz hit ships nowhere near this route.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: Ukraine's drones hit the Crimean Bridge that spans the strait, and a second strike within 24 hours dropped its road span. Both strikes came after the latest vessel count, so neither accounts for the recent rise in traffic, and nothing else reported from the strait explains it.

mkt:bist.standing: The 100 largest and most traded companies on Borsa İstanbul, Türkiye's only stock exchange. It is priced in lira, so the level carries the country's inflation as much as its earnings: read the direction, not the number.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The Kuala Lumpur Composite Index: the 30 largest companies on Bursa Malaysia, the national exchange in Kuala Lumpur. It is the world's largest market for Islamic finance instruments and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: Malaysia's fortnight ran to Najib Razak leaving Kajang prison for house arrest, scrutiny after the Nvidia scandal of the $94.67 billion in data centre investment approved since 2021, and a Taiwan investment freeze over Anwar's China line. None of it accounts for the index's fall.

mkt:idx.standing: Every company listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange in Jakarta, counted in one index. It is the market of the world's largest Muslim-majority country, and commodity producers and banks carry most of its weight.
mkt:idx.recent: The fortnight's news from Jakarta was political: Prabowo was said to accept the resignation of his vice president, a wiretap scandal raised the spectre of treason, and the rupiah fell to a record low as Fed bets boosted the dollar. None of it accounts for the index's longer slide.

mkt:tse.standing: The Nikkei 225 tracks 225 large companies on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, Japan's main market, weighted by share price. Tokyo is Asia's largest exchange and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: An AI rout spread to Asia, and South Korea halted trading after the Kospi fell 8%. A yen sliding toward 160 had lifted exporters, and nearly half of Japan's manufacturers raised profit forecasts. Then Japan spent a record ¥7.98 trillion in one day buying the yen back, and Washington sold euros for yen alongside it.

mkt:hkex.standing: The Hang Seng Index tracks the largest and most traded companies on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. It is where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital, and the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: The news from Hong Kong's biggest listed companies was mostly about AI spending and new listings: Tencent's surge in capital spending, Alibaba's plan to list its T-Head chip unit here, and JD.com's return to profit. None of it accounts for the index's fall.

mkt:sse.standing: The SSE Composite tracks every share listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange, mainland China's main board. Largely closed to foreign investors, it follows domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: The mainland stories of the period were about a yuan that has gained 9% on the euro and is squeezing exporters in Ningbo, producer prices at their highest since June 2022, and Washington pressing Beijing to carry out its Busan commitments. None of them names a cause for the slide.

mkt:krx.standing: The Korea Composite Stock Price Index: every company on the main board of the Korea Exchange in Seoul, weighted by size. Samsung and SK Hynix dominate it, so it moves with the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: A rout in AI stocks spread to Asia and hit Seoul hardest: South Korea halted trading on a Friday after the Kospi fell 8% in one session, dragging down SK Hynix with it. An Nvidia crisis was still clouding the chip race ten days later, even as SK Hynix pressed on with its first fab in Yongin.

mkt:bse.standing: The Sensitive Index: 30 of the largest companies on the Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai, India. The exchange is Asia's oldest, founded in 1875, and this index is the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: The fortnight's Indian news carried an export surge of 30% that narrowed October's trade deficit to $20.09 billion, and retail inflation of 6.09%, a two-year high that breached the ceiling. Neither is reported as the driver of the index's climb, and nothing in the input accounts for it.

mkt:sgx.standing: The 30 largest and most traded companies on the Singapore Exchange, the main market of Southeast Asia's financial hub. Three banks and regional property groups carry most of its weight, so it moves with interest rates.
mkt:sgx.recent: Singapore's news over the fortnight centred on the US criminal probe into Megaspeed, the Nvidia customer tied to Jensen Huang's exit, and on new US curbs on China's access to AI chips. Alongside it came a gold vault for foreign central banks and a DBS and JPMorgan deposit link, and none of it accounts for the index's fall.

mkt:twse.standing: The Taiwan Stock Exchange's capitalisation-weighted index of every common share listed in Taipei. TSMC alone is roughly a third of it, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: The AI rout that spread to Asia reached TSMC, the stock this index leans on, the day South Korea halted trading after the Kospi fell 8%. Xi pledged Taiwan's reunification, China staged unannounced Pacific drills the next day, and Micron paused work on a $4.5 billion Taiwan plant after the island's first chip-industry strike.

mkt:asx.standing: The 200 largest companies listed on the Australian Securities Exchange in Sydney, weighted by market value. Mining and banking dominate it, and it is often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: The fortnight carried a bond selloff on the risk of a half-point Fed hike, with two-year Treasury yields jumping 18 basis points overnight, and Coles disclosing a cyber attack without saying what happened. Neither is tied to this index's move in the reporting.

mkt:jse.standing: The All Share index covers nearly every company listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, South Africa's main market, weighted by size. It is Africa's largest exchange by far, and the only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: None of the fortnight's South African news accounts for the drop. It ran to a GDP rebasing that counted illegal miners, a slowdown at Woolworths Foods, and left parties naming their price for backing the ANC.

mkt:b3.standing: The most traded shares on B3, the São Paulo exchange that is Latin America's largest, weighted by market value. Iron ore, oil and Brazilian interest rates drive it, through the miners, oil producers and banks that dominate it.
mkt:b3.recent: Brazil's central bank said inflation had passed the top of its target range as growth slowed, citing four shocks; October consumer prices rose 4.63%, keeping pressure on rates. After the runoff the Senate passed the government's fiscal adjustment bill with 45 votes, and a softened sin tax spared industry for now.

mkt:bmv.standing: The Índice de Precios y Cotizaciones tracks about 35 of the largest, most traded companies on the Bolsa Mexicana de Valores in Mexico City. It is Mexico's benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: The run ended the day before Trump threatened to double tariffs on Mexico unless migrant caravans were stopped, after 1,500 migrants set out walking north from Tapachula. For an index whose companies sell into the US, a tariff tied to border politics rather than trade terms reaches straight into earnings.

mkt:byma.standing: Argentina's main stock index, on Bolsas y Mercados Argentinos in Buenos Aires. Priced in pesos, which have repeatedly lost most of their value, so it rises even in bad years: daily direction counts, the level does not.
mkt:byma.recent: The fortnight in Argentina brought Pope Leo's visit to a country where 32.3% of Argentines live in poverty, Javier Milei's refusal to recognise Lula's election win, and Iran's listing of the navy and air force as terrorist organisations. None of it accounts for the index's fall.

mkt:tsx.standing: The broad benchmark of the Toronto Stock Exchange, Canada's main market, tracking around 200 of its largest companies by market value. Banks, oil producers and miners dominate it, so it trades like a commodity index.
mkt:tsx.recent: The low came the day Carney said only US policy shifts could change Canada's trade stance, hours before meeting Trump in Shenzhen; two days earlier he had floated working with Chinese automakers if US trade talks fail. None of the reporting ties that standoff to the selloff itself.

mkt:nyse.standing: The S&P 500 tracks 500 of the largest companies listed on the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq, weighted by market value. It is the largest equity market on earth, and its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: Rate-hike bets returned: US consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, beating forecasts, and Fed minutes showed almost all officials expect more rate hikes. Nvidia spent the fortnight without Jensen Huang amid a spy scandal, and Washington closed a remote AI chip loophole used to reach China.

mkt:lse.standing: The 100 largest companies listed on the London Stock Exchange, Britain's main market, ranked by market value. Most of their revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.
mkt:lse.recent: The Bank of England raised rates and forecast inflation peaking at 4.9%, and Bailey said a second hike was more likely than not if the war went on. Inflation then accelerated again, firming the case for that second rise, and higher rates mean a stronger pound, which shrinks the sterling value of the index's foreign earnings.

mkt:xetra.standing: The Deutscher Aktienindex: the 40 largest companies on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, Germany's main market. It is built on the country's industrial and chemical base, making it Europe's clearest export barometer.
mkt:xetra.recent: Two of its own members carried the bad news: Mercedes-Benz halted investment in Germany after four months of talks, with its labour officials pledging to fight plant closures, and Deutsche Bank shares dropped on a leak of 15 million files showing it kept about 28,000 flagged clients. Brussels meanwhile cleared UniCredit's €45 billion bid for Commerzbank, another member.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: The 40 largest companies listed on Euronext Paris, France's main stock market, weighted by the value of their freely traded shares. Luxury and energy groups dominate it, leaving it unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: The fortnight's French news was political: Ifop puts Le Pen and Mélenchon ahead as the centre stalls, and Mélenchon promised nationalisations to a rally at Le Bourget. The European Central Bank then said markets, not it, should discipline France's debt, with the borrowing premium over Germany at 1.75 points.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The Amsterdam Exchange index tracks the largest, most traded companies on Euronext Amsterdam, the Dutch market. It is the world's oldest exchange, now carried largely by chip-equipment maker ASML.

mkt:bme.standing: The 35 most liquid companies on the Bolsa de Madrid, Spain's main stock exchange. Its big banks earn much of their profit in Latin America, so the index moves with both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: Spain's fortnight was dominated by its first general strike in 14 years, over housing, and by a Berlin deal giving Spain the European Central Bank presidency, with De Cos set to replace Lagarde. Neither story accounts for the index's path.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: The 40 largest, most traded companies on Borsa Italiana in Milan, Italy's main market. Banks and utilities dominate it, making it the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: The fortnight's news reached the index's heaviest sector twice: Rome wants €5.9 billion from its banks next year, a levy Intesa attacked, and UniCredit's €45 billion bid for Commerzbank won unconditional EU approval. Neither accounts for the price.

mkt:six.standing: The Swiss Market Index: the 20 largest companies on the SIX Swiss Exchange in Zurich, Switzerland's main market. Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry it, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.
mkt:six.recent: The fortnight's news from Switzerland was diplomatic rather than corporate: Moscow aired its concerns over Switzerland's OSCE chairmanship, and its embassy said Swiss policy had buried the country's reputation as a mediator. None of it reaches Nestlé, Roche or Novartis, and none of it accounts for the index.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: The OMX Stockholm 30: the 30 most traded shares on Nasdaq Stockholm, Sweden's main stock exchange. Nordic industrials and telecoms weigh heavily in it, which makes it a useful early read on European capital spending.

mkt:tase.standing: The 125 largest companies by market value on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, Israel's only stock market. It trades Sunday to Thursday and is heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.
mkt:tase.recent: None of the fortnight's news gives a market reason for the decline. It ran alongside an unsettled Israel: a Knesset sworn in with Benjamin Netanyahu keeping command as caretaker without a majority, Eisenkot weighing a unity government with him, and Israel's first large ground operation in central Gaza since the ceasefire.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: The number of people who open the Wikipedia article on Donald Trump, the US president, each day. It rises when he does something readers want to look up, a rough gauge of how far American politics is reaching a general audience.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: Trump went to Shenzhen for a summit with Xi and Putin at which Ukraine, Europe and Japan had no seat. In Brooklyn, Asif Merchant was sentenced to 330 months for plotting to kill him, and a Deutsche Bank memo tied two Trump companies to laundromats. All of this came well after the early-month peak, and nothing in the input explains that peak.

fed-funds.standing: The range the Federal Reserve sets for overnight lending between US banks. Every dollar borrowing cost is priced off it, from mortgages and Treasury yields to the debts of governments and companies far outside the United States.
fed-funds.recent: The Fed held at its October 27-28 meeting, but the minutes show almost all officials expect more hikes, with inflation pushed up by the oil shock. October consumer prices rose 0.4%, Logan called for two more hikes, and traders put 78% odds on a December move.

ecb-rate.standing: The interest the European Central Bank pays commercial banks on money parked with it overnight, and the rate that steers borrowing costs across the euro zone. Mortgages, business loans and government bond yields move after it.
ecb-rate.recent: None of the fortnight's news moved the rate; it was about who sets it. Germany won the chief economist seat for Markus Brunnermeier and Spain the presidency for De Cos, succeeding Christine Lagarde. The European Central Bank also left France to markets as its borrowing premium over Germany hit 1.75 points.

us-unemployment.standing: The share of the American labour force without a job and actively looking for one, from a monthly household survey. It is one half of the Federal Reserve's mandate, so interest rates move with it.
us-unemployment.recent: Hiring ran well ahead of what forecasters expected: US employers added 165,000 jobs in October, against 65,000 forecast. Prices rose only slightly over the same month, and Fed officials, Barkin among them, called the policy direction clear while urging a careful pace.

xag.standing: The price of a troy ounce of silver on New York's COMEX futures market. It is part precious metal and part industrial input, used in solar panels and electronics, so it moves with gold and with factory demand.
xag.recent: Silver fell with gold, which hit $3,757 an ounce, its lowest since September 2025, as the Fed signalled more rate hikes and the dollar firmed. Higher rates raise the cost of holding metals that pay no interest. The slide came after gold had held above $4,000 on the midterm result earlier in the month.

us-cpi.standing: The yearly rise in the Consumer Price Index, the Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly measure of what American households pay. The Federal Reserve sets interest rates against it, and borrowing costs worldwide follow.
us-cpi.recent: October's report showed inflation slowing less than expected, and the Fed's Goolsbee called it 'borderline disturbing'. Treasuries slid as traders cemented bets on a December rate hike, and Bitcoin dropped to almost a three-month low as the data dimmed risk appetite.

portwatch-hormuz-tanker.standing: A daily count of oil tankers passing the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow channel between Iran and Oman. About a fifth of the world's oil leaves the Gulf through it, so a drop here reaches fuel prices in Asia first.
portwatch-hormuz-tanker.recent: Mines, not a blockade, emptied the strait: Iran's Guard said mines hit tankers day after day, and Acting US Navy Secretary Hung Cao told senators one transit now costs $64m to insure. In Islamabad, Iran shortened its reopening plan from 7 days to 2, while Pakistan's mango earnings fell from $100 million to $60 million.

portwatch-bab-container.standing: Container ships crossing the strait between Yemen and Djibouti each day, the southern gate of the Red Sea and the Suez route between Asia and Europe. When it is unsafe, lines divert around Africa and freight takes weeks longer.
portwatch-bab-container.recent: Yemeni government forces withdrew from the coast by the strait, leaving the Houthis holding the Red Sea's southern chokepoint as they pushed on toward Aden. The same week a Japanese container ship transited for the first time in three years, while Houthi missiles kept reaching Riyadh and Saudi-led strikes hit Hodeidah.

portwatch-suez-total.standing: The number of ships passing each day through Egypt's canal between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea, the short route between Asia and Europe. When it falls, cargo is going round Africa, adding days and fuel to every voyage.
portwatch-suez-total.recent: Yemen's government forces withdrew from the Bab el-Mandeb coast and the Houthis took it, putting the Red Sea's southern chokepoint, the far end of the route through Suez, in the hands of a group now pressing Aden. That came as these readings end, and nothing reported in the fortnight accounts for the earlier climb in traffic.

portwatch-panama-total.standing: Ships crossing the Panama Canal each day, the shortcut between the Atlantic and the Pacific. Its locks run on fresh water from Gatún Lake, so drought in Panama cuts the daily slots and delays trade between Asia and the US east coast.
portwatch-panama-total.recent: The fortnight's news from Panama was about Etesa, whose $35.9 million transmission contract with Iverco grew to $154.6 million, and the bombing of journalist Rolando Rodríguez's home; none of it touches the canal or accounts for its traffic.

portwatch-malacca-total.standing: The count of ships passing each day through the strait between Malaysia and Indonesia's Sumatra, the shortest sea route from the Indian Ocean to the Pacific. Most oil East Asia imports from the Middle East goes through it.

portwatch-taiwan-total.standing: The count of cargo ships and tankers passing each day between Taiwan and mainland China. The strait is the main lane between the ports of north-east Asia and the routes south, and typhoons and military drills both empty it.

portwatch-dover-total.standing: The narrowest part of the English Channel, between England and France, and one of the busiest shipping lanes in the world. Most cargo sailing between the Atlantic and the ports of northern Europe passes through it.
portwatch-dover-total.recent: The news from either side of the strait was about France's Yellow Vest protests over the cost of living, a cyberattack on French supermarket freezers that prosecutors blame on Iran, and US aircraft leaving RAF Mildenhall. None of it involved ships or ports, and none of it explains the traffic.

portwatch-gibraltar-total.standing: The count of ships passing each day through the 14-kilometre gap between Spain and Morocco, the only sea route between the Atlantic and the Mediterranean. Traffic bound to or from the Suez Canal passes here too.
portwatch-gibraltar-total.recent: The fortnight's news from the sea lanes was about the Gulf and the Red Sea. Iran says mines hit tankers in Hormuz, and the Houthis now hold the Red Sea's southern chokepoint at Bab el-Mandeb. None of it accounts for traffic through Gibraltar.

wiki-ukraine.standing: How many times a day Wikipedia's article on Ukraine is opened. Readers arrive when the country's war with Russia, its grain exports or its diplomacy turn up in the news, so the count marks when the world looks its way.
wiki-ukraine.recent: Russia and Ukraine held their first peace talks in 9 months in Abu Dhabi, where, Zelensky says, the US raised a Donbas withdrawal in exchange for NATO. Ukrainian drones then hit the Kerch bridge to Crimea, Russia struck bridges in Kyiv, and Brussels proposed a €45 billion loan repayable only if Russia pays reparations.

xmr.standing: A cryptocurrency built to hide the sender, receiver and amount of every transaction. That privacy makes it the coin of choice for ransomware crews and darknet markets, and the one exchanges delist under regulatory pressure.

co:nvidia.standing: Designs the processors that most artificial-intelligence models are trained and run on, and sells them to the companies building data centres. It designs chips and does not make them: TSMC does.
co:nvidia.recent: Jensen Huang quit after scrutiny of his ties to Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive at the centre of a US-China spy scandal; Colette Kress now runs the company. Chinese buyers stockpiled its chips ahead of an expected US crackdown. Results that doubled profit to $65.3 billion, with a $130bn quarter forecast, did not halt the fall.

co:apple.standing: Makes the iPhone, which brings in about half its sales, along with Mac computers, iPads and watches, and takes a cut of what is sold through its App Store.
co:apple.recent: Apple's iPhone AI in China launched running on Alibaba's Qwen rather than a model of its own, and every Mac since 2022 turned out to build a graph of its owner's relationships. Later its services went down, which Apple put down to an internal update. None of it accounts for the share price.

co:alphabet.standing: Owns Google and YouTube. Most of its money comes from advertising beside search results and videos; it also sells cloud computing and builds its own AI models.
co:alphabet.recent: The company's own news since the trough was of spending and shipping: a $10 billion stake in Anthropic ahead of its IPO, a pledge to take over Anthropic's $19 billion data center lease that let TeraWulf borrow on Google's credit, two more Gemini 4 models, and a judge's approval to buy Spirit Airlines' passenger data. None of it explains the earlier fall.

co:amazon.standing: An online retailer, and through Amazon Web Services the largest seller of cloud computing, which earns most of its profit.
co:amazon.recent: The one event in the window about Amazon's own business was a setback: a Vulcan rocket from United Launch Alliance, the Boeing and Lockheed Martin venture, failed minutes after launch from Cape Canaveral and destroyed 40 Amazon Leo satellites. Nothing in the input accounts for the share's path.

co:tsmc.standing: Manufactures the chips other companies design, among them Apple’s, Nvidia’s and AMD’s, and makes most of the world’s most advanced ones, in Taiwan.

co:microsoft.standing: Sells Windows and Office, and rents out computing power through Azure, one of the largest clouds. It holds a large stake in OpenAI.
co:microsoft.recent: Outlook and Teams went down for nearly a day, Downdetector logged 130,000 outage reports at the peak, and the shares fell by 3% as offices worldwide lost mail. The same week a researcher leaked SignDrop, a Windows exploit giving ordinary users System rights. Earlier, Nvidia's 6.27% fall briefly let Microsoft pass it in market value.

co:broadcom.standing: Makes the networking chips that connect data centres and designs custom AI chips for companies such as Google. It also owns the software firm VMware.
co:broadcom.recent: Anthropic's S-1 filing was read as strengthening the case for Broadcom's AI growth, because it put a large AI developer's spending plans on the record for a company that designs chips for exactly that kind of buyer. Nothing else in the input speaks to Broadcom's own results, orders or rulings.

co:spacex.standing: Builds reusable rockets, launches satellites and astronauts for governments and companies, and runs Starlink, a satellite internet network.
co:spacex.recent: The low came as SpaceX's default risk hit a fresh peak in a tech-led selloff. The recovery ran through a plan for $74 billion in AI computing campuses and the first tower catch of a Starship upper stage, Ship 42, after 14 orbits. Meanwhile Brussels demanded that Starshield be restored to Ukraine's drones, a charge SpaceX denies.

co:meta.standing: Owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, used by more than three billion people, and earns nearly all its money from advertising on them.
co:meta.recent: Meta drew a run of penalties without a change to its advertising business: Italy fined it $880m over photo privacy, Brazil fined Facebook for 9 days of missed court orders, and Meta shelved terms claiming AI training rights over its customers' websites. None of it explains the share's swing.

co:aramco.standing: Saudi Arabia’s state oil company, which pumps more oil than any other company. The government owns nearly all of it, and its dividends pay for much of the kingdom’s budget.
co:aramco.recent: The Houthis claimed 6 strikes inside Saudi Arabia. Debris from intercepted missiles then blew out windows across Aramco Tower in Riyadh, and an unclaimed attack set the East-West pipeline ablaze, the line that carries crude across the kingdom. The Yemeni military has since named Aramco its prime target. None of this accounts for the share price.

co:tesla.standing: Makes electric cars, and the batteries that store power for homes and electricity grids. Led by Elon Musk, who also leads SpaceX.
co:tesla.recent: Tesla ended the Cybertruck after selling 11,586 in nine months, by Cox Automotive's estimate, and the shares jumped 4% that morning on the steering-wheel-free Cybercab meant to replace it. Days later it opened Cybercab orders, and Bloomberg reported SpaceX–Tesla merger talks aimed at December.

co:samsung.standing: One of the three companies that make most of the world’s memory chips, and one of the largest makers of smartphones and televisions.
co:samsung.recent: Samsung was reported to be in buyout talks for Modine, and a week earlier was building for the AI boom; neither accounts for the fall in its shares.

co:micron.standing: The one large American maker of memory chips, the kind that hold data in phones, computers and AI data centres. Its two main rivals are Samsung and SK Hynix.
co:micron.recent: Micron fell 11% on the day chip stocks slid after the midterms, and the same day brought trouble of its own. About 12 workers in Taoyuan staged Taiwan's first chip-industry strike, and Micron paused work on its $4.5 Billion Taiwan plant after the labor spat.

co:amd.standing: Designs processors for computers and data centres, where it competes with Intel, and AI chips, where it competes with Nvidia. Like Nvidia, it has TSMC make them.
co:amd.recent: The trough came in the chip selloff after the midterms, when a backlash against data centres hit the companies that sell into them. AMD fell 12% that Thursday, twice Nvidia's 6% drop and worse than Micron's 11%, because data-centre processors and AI chips are where its growth is priced.

co:berkshire.standing: A holding company built by Warren Buffett. It owns insurers, a railway and energy utilities outright, and holds large stakes in companies such as Apple and Coca-Cola.
co:berkshire.recent: The one story in the window about Berkshire itself was Buffett giving 9 million of his own shares to family foundations. The gift changes who holds the stock, not what the company earns, and nothing in the input explains the climb in the share price.

co:lilly.standing: An American drugmaker. Its diabetes and weight-loss medicines, sold as Mounjaro and Zepbound, account for much of its growth.

co:jpmorgan.standing: The largest bank in the United States by assets, serving households, companies and governments.
co:jpmorgan.recent: Chase's systems failed on Monday for nearly 5,000 customers by Downdetector's count, with Zelle payments delayed, in a week when Microsoft, the FAA and Apple Pay also went down. The same day JPMorgan linked its blockchain deposit network with DBS for 24/7 dollar transfers.

co:skhynix.standing: A South Korean maker of memory chips, and the main supplier of the high-speed memory that Nvidia’s AI chips need.
co:skhynix.recent: The only news on SK Hynix in the fortnight was its round-the-clock push to finish its first fab in Yongin, a plant that will stand 150 metres tall. None of it explains why the share fell.

co:walmart.standing: The world’s largest retailer by sales, with thousands of stores in the United States and abroad.

co:asml.standing: A Dutch company, and the only maker of the machines needed to print the most advanced chips. Every leading chipmaker buys from it, and its sales to China are restricted.

us-2y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for two years. Of all Treasury yields it follows the Federal Reserve's policy rate most closely, so it shows where traders are betting that rate goes next.

us-mortgage.standing: The average interest rate US lenders charge on a 30-year fixed home loan, the mortgage most American buyers take. It follows long-dated Treasury yields, and it sets what a house costs each month and whether owners can afford to move.
us-mortgage.recent: The one related report in the fortnight was that home sales in the US had fallen to their lowest level since 2016. That is a symptom of expensive borrowing, not a cause of it, and nothing reported in the window accounts for the rate's rise.

ez-cpi.standing: The annual rise in consumer prices across the countries that share the euro, measured by Eurostat on one harmonised basket. The European Central Bank aims for 2% and sets the bloc's interest rates against it.

bnb.standing: The native token of BNB Chain, the blockchain network built by the exchange Binance. Holders use it to pay transaction fees on the chain and get trading discounts on Binance, so its price follows the exchange's fortunes and its regulators.

trx.standing: The token of the Tron blockchain, a network built for cheap, fast transfers. Most of its traffic is the dollar stablecoin Tether, so its price follows demand for moving dollars outside banks, especially in emerging markets.

sol.standing: The token of the Solana blockchain, used to pay its transaction fees and staked by the validators that secure it. Its price is a bet on how much trading and payment traffic the network wins, and it swings harder than Bitcoin.
sol.recent: The trough came the same day Bitcoin fell below $65,000 for the first time since August, a slide that took the wider crypto market down with it. No news in this window points to anything specific to Solana's own network or its backers.

xrp.standing: The native token of the XRP Ledger, a payments network built for fast cross-border transfers. Ripple, the company most closely tied to it, holds a large share of the supply, so its legal and commercial fortunes move the price.
xrp.recent: XRP fell with the whole crypto market. An Nvidia-led tech selloff hit the crypto majors, US inflation data pushed Bitcoin to almost a three-month low, and outflows from Bitcoin ETFs mounted. As money left crypto, XRP reached its lowest price since November 2024.

hype.standing: The token of Hyperliquid, a blockchain built to run a derivatives exchange where traders bet on crypto prices with leverage. Trading fees fund buybacks of the token, so its price follows how much business the exchange does.
hype.recent: Nvidia's perpetual futures on Hyperliquid fell 7% after reports that the board may oust Jensen Huang, and a former Robinhood engineer pleaded guilty to an insider trading scheme run on the exchange. Neither event accounts for the token's slide.

doge.standing: A cryptocurrency launched as a joke around a Shiba Inu dog meme, with no cap on how many coins can exist. It has little use beyond payments and tipping, so its price moves on online attention and celebrity endorsement.

zec.standing: A cryptocurrency built on Bitcoin's design, with the same 21 million coin cap, that lets users hide sender, receiver and amount using zero-knowledge proofs. It is the main market price put on financial privacy on a public blockchain.
zec.recent: Zcash jumped 12% in a post-election crypto rebound that kept Bitcoin above $80,000, the run that carried it to its peak. Nothing reported in the weeks since accounts for the slide that followed.

boe-rate.standing: Bank Rate, the interest the Bank of England pays commercial banks on their reserves, set by its nine-member Monetary Policy Committee. British mortgage, savings and business loan rates are priced off it, and sterling moves with it.
boe-rate.recent: The Bank of England raised rates this month for the first time since 2023, unanimously, and forecast that Britain's inflation would peak at 4.9%. October's figure then accelerated to 3.6%, and both Bailey and the Bank's chief economist said further rises were needed, Bailey calling a second hike more likely than not if the war goes on.

link.standing: The token of Chainlink, a network of oracles that feeds outside data such as prices into blockchain smart contracts. Node operators are paid in it, and much of decentralised lending relies on its price feeds.

boj-rate.standing: The Bank of Japan's short-term policy rate, the price of overnight money in yen. Kept near zero for decades, it made the yen the world's cheapest currency to borrow, so a rise pulls money back to Japan from markets everywhere.
boj-rate.recent: The yen's slide toward 160 per dollar is the pressure on this rate: Japan spent a record ¥7.98 trillion buying yen in one day, and wholesale inflation accelerated. BOJ chief Ueda sees 'some upside risks' to inflation. Households still resist higher prices, though: Uniqlo reversed a sock price increase within days.

tcmb-rate.standing: The one-week repo rate at which the Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye lends to commercial banks, and the country's main policy rate. It sets the cost of lira credit and shapes how attractive the currency is to hold against inflation.
tcmb-rate.recent: The one relevant item from the fortnight is the central bank raising its end-2027 inflation forecast to 21%, published after the latest reading. A higher inflation path argues for a slower pace of cuts, but nothing in the input explains the cut itself.

pboc-rate.standing: The one-year loan prime rate, the benchmark the People's Bank of China steers and that banks use to price most new business and household loans. It sets the cost of credit across the world's second-largest economy.
pboc-rate.recent: The fortnight's news from the People's Bank of China concerned the yuan abroad, not borrowing costs at home. The PBOC opened the digital yuan, which has handled 31 trillion yuan, to overseas lenders, and Beijing planned debut yuan bond sales in Canada. None of it bears on the rate.

bcb-rate.standing: The Selic, the overnight rate the Central Bank of Brazil sets to steer inflation toward its target. It prices government debt and bank lending across Latin America's largest economy, and the real's appeal to foreign money rises and falls with it.
bcb-rate.recent: Brazil's central bank is caught between two pressures: inflation has passed the top of its target range while growth slows. The bank names four separate shocks behind the overshoot, so it cannot ease to support a cooling economy without letting prices run further.

bi-rate.standing: The rate Bank Indonesia sets for seven-day lending to commercial banks, its main policy tool. It steers borrowing costs across Southeast Asia's largest economy and is used to defend the rupiah when capital flows out.
bi-rate.recent: The latest news on Indonesia's money concerned the currency rather than the rate: the rupiah fell to a record low as Fed bets boosted the dollar, the pressure that limits how far Bank Indonesia can cut. Nothing in it reports a rate decision.

cbr-rate.standing: The Bank of Russia's key rate, the price at which it lends to and takes deposits from commercial banks for a week. Rouble mortgages, company loans and the government's own borrowing costs are all priced off it.
cbr-rate.recent: On November 5 the Bank of Russia raised the path it projects for its key rate, forecasting fourth-quarter inflation of 7.1-7.6%. It tied that higher trajectory to bringing inflation to 4% in 2027, which keeps borrowing in Russia dearer for longer than the bank had signalled before.

mkt:set.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of every common stock on the Stock Exchange of Thailand in Bangkok, the country's main market. It is sensitive to tourism flows and regional energy prices.
mkt:set.recent: Two developments bore on Thai companies: Siam Cement kept its core Vietnam plastics plant, shut by the Hormuz disruption, closed until mid-2027, and Thai inflation hit 3.9%, above the central bank's ceiling. Neither, on its own, accounts for the index's fall.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Tadawul All Share Index covers every company on the Saudi Exchange's main market in Riyadh, the Arab world's largest by value and dominated by Aramco. It trades Sunday to Thursday, opening the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: A Houthi strike on Riyadh's airport killed at least 13 on 10 October. Then an unclaimed attack set the East-West pipeline ablaze, and debris from intercepted missiles blew out windows across Aramco Tower. Oil output kept climbing regardless: Saudi Arabia pumped 10.56 million barrels a day in October, up 26%.

mkt:dfm.standing: The main index of the Dubai Financial Market, the stock exchange in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. It is the Gulf's main listing venue for property and banking, and trades Monday to Friday, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: The fortnight's Dubai news was Swissaid's finding that the UAE remained the top destination for smuggled African gold. The region's was Trump signalling after a Qatar meeting that new Iran strikes were unnecessary. Neither is tied to the property and banking firms this index is built on, and none of it accounts for the price.

mkt:pse.standing: The PSEi tracks 30 large companies listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange in Manila, the country's only bourse. It is a small, domestically driven market, and remittance flows from Filipinos working abroad move the index.
mkt:pse.recent: The fortnight brought Manila a run of summitry: Trump announced a trade deal with the Philippines and critical-mineral deals at the Quad, and Marcos left for APEC in Shenzhen. None of it accounts for the index's slide.

stocks:META.standing: The owner of Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, which earns nearly all its revenue selling ads to reach more than three billion daily users. Its spending on AI data centres is among the heaviest in the industry.
stocks:META.recent: Meta took a run of legal and regulatory blows: Italy fined it $880m over photo privacy, Brazil fined Facebook for missed court orders, four nonprofits sued to freeze its next AI models, and it shelved terms claiming training rights over customers' websites. None of it accounts for the fall in the share.

poly-will-pedro-sanchez-be-the-next-prim.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Pedro Sánchez, Spain's Socialist prime minister, heads the government formed after the next general election. The price is what traders pay for a yes, and it moves on polls, coalition arithmetic and court cases.

stocks:0700.HK.standing: The Shenzhen company behind WeChat, the app most of China uses to message and pay, and the world's largest video-game publisher by revenue. Its Hong Kong share is one of the heaviest weights in the Hang Seng index.
stocks:0700.HK.recent: Tencent spent to meet AI demand while cutting what it charges for it. It expanded Hy4 inference capacity tenfold as WorkBuddy demand surged, then priced Hy4 flash at $0.07 per million input tokens, a 95% cut in task costs. Quarterly figures released after the low showed capital spending up 528% to 81.4 billion yuan.

stocks:NVDA.standing: The American designer of the graphics processors that train and run most of the world's AI models. Data-centre chips earn most of its revenue, so its share price is read as a gauge of what the industry spends on AI.
stocks:NVDA.recent: The slide follows Jensen Huang's exit after an email confessing an affair with a Singapore-based company's CEO, and a criminal probe into Megaspeed over diverting Nvidia chips. A shareholder lawsuit and a US rule closing the remote AI chip loophole to China followed; a quarter that doubled profit to $65.3 billion did not halt it.

poly-will-rebeca-grynspan-be-the-next-se.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Rebeca Grynspan, the Costa Rican economist heading UN Trade and Development, becomes the next UN Secretary-General. The Security Council's five veto holders must all accept the nominee.
poly-will-rebeca-grynspan-be-the-next-se.recent: The fortnight's news about Polymarket concerned the platform itself, with Trump Jr. leaving Kalshi after his firm invested $300 million in its rival, and none of it touches the race for the UN's top job or explains the swings in this contract.

poly-edi-rama-out-as-albania-pm-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Edi Rama stops being Albania's prime minister before the end of 2026. Rama, leader of the Socialist Party, took office in 2013.

stocks:GOOGL.standing: The parent company of Google, earning most of its revenue from search and YouTube advertising, alongside Google Cloud and Waymo. Its share is a running bet on whether AI assistants strengthen or erode the search ad business.
stocks:GOOGL.recent: Google shipped Hydrogen and then Neon, its fourth Gemini 4 model in 7 weeks. A judge approved its deal to train AI on Spirit Airlines' estimated 100 million emails, and it bought $10 billion of Anthropic alongside Nvidia. All of this came after the share's slide, and none of it explains the fall.

poly-saudi-houthi-ceasefire-agreement-an.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis agree a ceasefire before the year ends. Its price is what traders pay for a yes, and it moves with strikes, mediation and the Red Sea shipping the war hangs over.
poly-saudi-houthi-ceasefire-agreement-an.recent: The war widened instead of pausing: Houthi missile debris blew out windows across Aramco Tower in Riyadh, an unclaimed attack set the East-West pipeline ablaze, and the Houthis said they targeted King Khalid Airport. Saudi-led strikes hit Hodeidah as Houthi forces pushed toward Aden, seat of the internationally recognised government.

poly-will-a-us-iran-deal-in-2026-include.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether a US-Iran agreement reached in 2026 has Iran hand over its stockpile of enriched uranium, the material at the centre of the nuclear dispute and of any settlement between the two.
poly-will-a-us-iran-deal-in-2026-include.recent: Nothing since has pointed toward a deal. The US bombed Qeshm Island, Iran's base at the mouth of the Strait of Hormuz, and Tehran answered by striking Kuwait and Bahrain while peace talks stalled. The only diplomacy on record, in Islamabad, was about reopening the strait, not about uranium.

poly-will-deepseek-ipo-by-december-31-20.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if DeepSeek, the Hangzhou AI lab spun out of the hedge fund High-Flyer, lists its shares before 2028. A listing would open China's most closely watched AI lab to public shareholders.

poly-venezuela-election-scheduled-by-dec.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Venezuela's authorities formally schedule a national election before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will stake on a vote being called, not on one being held.

poly-will-any-country-join-the-mecca-agr.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if any further country formally joins the Mecca Agreement before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will stake on the pact widening beyond its founding signatories.

poly-will-peter-obi-win-the-2027-nigeria.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Peter Obi, the former Anambra governor who ran third in 2023, wins Nigeria's presidency in 2027. Its price is what traders will pay on an opposition upset of the ruling APC.
poly-will-peter-obi-win-the-2027-nigeria.recent: Nigeria's pre-election news turned on the conduct of the vote rather than the candidates: the electoral commission blamed 54 officials for fake voter records, and armed men blocked Isa Pantami's convoy in Gombe with burning tyres. Neither story bears on Obi's own chances or explains the price.

poly-sudan-civil-war-ceasefire-by-decemb.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Sudan's army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces agree a ceasefire before 2026 ends. The war, fought since April 2023, has driven the world's largest displacement crisis.

poly-russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-agreemen.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Russia and Ukraine agree a ceasefire before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on talks, envoys and sanctions decisions.
poly-russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-agreemen.recent: Russia and Ukraine held their first peace talks in 9 months, but the message from Abu Dhabi was that Putin is not ready to make peace. Zelensky then said the US had raised a Donbas withdrawal in exchange for NATO entry, while strikes escalated: Ukraine hit the Kerch bridge and Russia damaged the bridges of Kyiv.

poly-will-no-qualifying-diplomatic-us-ir.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if no senior American and Iranian officials meet before 2026 ends. The two governments have met at that level only rarely since 1979, so a meeting would break a long pattern.
poly-will-no-qualifying-diplomatic-us-ir.recent: The war widened: after the US bombed Qeshm Island, Iran struck an airbase used by US forces in Kuwait and hit Bahrain 4 times in 6 days, and a third US carrier reached the Gulf. Mediation in Islamabad yielded only a shorter Hormuz reopening plan, and peace talks are stalled.

poly-openai-1t-valuation-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT, reaches a valuation of at least $1 trillion in 2026. OpenAI is privately held, so this is a rare public wager on what the AI boom's best-known lab is worth.

poly-moodys-or-sp-downgrades-france-by-n.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Moody's or S&P cuts France's sovereign credit rating before its deadline. Those ratings feed into what Paris pays to borrow and which funds can hold its bonds.

poly-will-gyanesh-kumar-be-out-as-chief-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Gyanesh Kumar leaves office as India's Chief Election Commissioner by the deadline. The post runs national and state votes, and removal requires the same process as for a Supreme Court judge.
poly-will-gyanesh-kumar-be-out-as-chief-.recent: What India news there was in the fortnight concerned the Modi government, with a protest at Jantar Mantar calling for it to be ousted through the ballot box. None of it touched the Election Commission or Gyanesh Kumar, and none of it accounts for what traders now pay on this contract.

poly-will-iran-withdraw-from-the-npt-bef.standing: A Polymarket contract on Iran formally quitting the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty by 2027. The treaty lets a member leave on three months' notice, and leaving would end the legal basis for inspections of Iran's sites.
poly-will-iran-withdraw-from-the-npt-bef.recent: The fortnight's reporting on Iran was about the war, not the treaty: Iranian fire on Kuwait and Bahrain after the US struck Qeshm Island, and tankers mined in the Strait of Hormuz. None of it touched Iran's place in the NPT, and none of it accounts for the bet's fall.

poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if U.S. forces invade Iran before 2027; its price is what traders will pay for that outcome. It asks about an invasion, a far higher bar than an air or missile strike.
poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.recent: The war here is fought from the air and sea: the US bombed Qeshm Island, Iran struck Bahrain and Kuwait, mines hit tankers in Hormuz and a third US carrier reached the Gulf, none of it an invasion. JD Vance blamed the Iran war for Trump's midterm defeat.

poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States ends its blockade of Iran by the close of 2026. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, which is tied to whether Gulf oil reaches its importers.
poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.recent: The US bombed Qeshm Island, Iran's base at the mouth of the Strait of Hormuz, and Iran answered by hitting Kuwait and Bahrain, which host US forces. A third US carrier reached the Gulf, Iran said mines hit 4 tankers, and peace talks stalled, even after Iran shortened its Hormuz reopening plan from 7 days to 2.

poly-israel-x-hamas-ceasefire-cancelled-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Israel-Hamas ceasefire is cancelled by Dec 31. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it reacts to fighting in Gaza and to the politics of the governments behind the truce.
poly-israel-x-hamas-ceasefire-cancelled-.recent: The truce frayed without being called off: an Israeli airstrike killed 6 people inside Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis, Israel then launched central Gaza's first large operation since the ceasefire, and the Board of Peace, the truce's overseer, warned of collapse while blaming both Israel and Hamas.

poly-us-iran-hormuz-agreement-by-decembe.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the United States and Iran reach an agreement on the Strait of Hormuz by December 31. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, on a waterway that Gulf energy exporters and importers depend on.
poly-us-iran-hormuz-agreement-by-decembe.recent: Talks stalled as the fighting widened. Iran says mines hit 4 tankers in 24 hours, and a third US carrier joined 13 destroyers facing Iran. After the US bombed Qeshm Island, Tehran struck Kuwait and Bahrain. Acting US Navy Secretary Hung Cao told senators that insuring one transit now costs $64m.

poly-will-the-fed-increase-interest-rate.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Federal Reserve raises its policy rate by a quarter point at its December meeting. That rate anchors short-term dollar borrowing, so bonds, mortgages and currencies worldwide reprice around it.
poly-will-the-fed-increase-interest-rate.recent: October consumer prices rose 0.4%, beating forecasts, and the bet swung from hold to hike. Logan called for two more rate hikes, Deutsche Bank forecast a run of them, and Waller said the Fed should consider a half-point move. Then the minutes showed almost all officials expect more hikes.

poly-us-iran-hormuz-agreement-by-novembe.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Washington and Tehran reach an agreement on the Strait of Hormuz by November 30. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, on the waterway that carries Gulf oil and gas to the world.
poly-us-iran-hormuz-agreement-by-novembe.recent: Peace talks stalled as the war widened. The US bombed Qeshm Island, Iran's base at the mouth of the strait, and Iran answered with strikes on Kuwait and Bahrain. Iran says mines hit four tankers in 24 hours, a third US carrier reached the Gulf, and insuring a single transit now costs $64m.

poly-strait-of-hormuz-traffic-returns-to.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if shipping through the Strait of Hormuz returns to normal by December 31. Roughly a fifth of the world's oil passes the strait, so the price is a bet on Gulf supply reopening.
poly-strait-of-hormuz-traffic-returns-to.recent: Mines, not a declared blockade, are emptying the strait. Iran says mines hit 4 tankers in 24 hours, and Acting US Navy Secretary Hung Cao put insurance on one transit at $64m. In Islamabad, Iran shortened its reopening plan from 7 days to 2, but it still ties the strait to seven conditions, and the attacks went on.

poly-will-ukraine-sign-an-eu-accession-t.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Ukraine signs its EU accession treaty by 2027. Signing comes only after every negotiating chapter closes and all 27 member states agree, so the price is a bet on the pace of talks in Brussels.
poly-will-ukraine-sign-an-eu-accession-t.recent: The fortnight's reporting on Ukraine ran through the Abu Dhabi peace talks, the US suggestion that Kyiv cede Donbas for NATO entry, and a €45 billion EU loan repayable only if Russia pays reparations. None of it touched the accession treaty itself.

poly-pete-hegseth-out-as-secretary-of-de.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Pete Hegseth stops being the US Secretary of Defense before the end of the year. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on reports about his standing at the Pentagon.

wiki-inflation.standing: The general rise in prices across an economy, usually measured by a consumer price index. Central banks set interest rates to keep it near a target, so its pace decides what borrowers and savers pay.
wiki-inflation.recent: The Bank of England raised rates unanimously and warned of 4.9% inflation, with Bailey saying a second hike was more likely than not if the war goes on. US consumer prices then rose 0.4% in October, beating forecasts, India's retail inflation hit 6.09%, a two-year high, and Fed minutes showed almost all officials expect more rate hikes.

wiki-china.standing: How many people open Wikipedia's article on China each day: a rough gauge of how often the world's second-largest economy and most populous one-party state pulls general readers toward the basics.
wiki-china.recent: The latest stories about China cover its push to settle nearly 30% of goods trade in yuan, its accusation that Chile and Belgium struck a backroom deal over the High Seas Treaty secretariat, and a US rule closing a remote AI chip loophole. None of them dates from the late-October peak, so none accounts for it.

poly-houthi-x-saudi-arabia-effective-cea.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Houthis and Saudi Arabia agree a ceasefire before the year ends. Its price is what traders will pay on the war between Yemen's Houthi movement and the kingdom ending, and so on Red Sea and Gulf oil risk.
poly-houthi-x-saudi-arabia-effective-cea.recent: The war moved onto Saudi soil. Missile debris blew out windows across Aramco Tower, an unclaimed attack set the East-West pipeline ablaze, and the Houthis claimed a strike on King Khalid Airport. Saudi-led strikes hit Hodeidah in reply, while Houthi forces pushed toward Aden, the seat of the internationally recognised government.

wiki-islamic-revolutionary-guard-corps.standing: The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps is Iran's parallel military, founded after the 1979 revolution and answerable to the Supreme Leader. It runs the missile force, a navy in the Gulf and a large business empire.
wiki-islamic-revolutionary-guard-corps.recent: The Guard claimed drone strikes on a US radar in Bahrain, the third Iranian attack there in a week, and said tankers taking its banned Hormuz route had hit mines and burned. In Paris, prosecutors blamed it for hacking freezers in 700 French supermarkets.

wiki-united-states.standing: Daily reads of English Wikipedia's article on the United States, one of its most-visited country pages. It rises when American power or politics becomes the world's story, not only America's.
wiki-united-states.recent: Nine flipped seats, Peltola's in Alaska among them, gave Democrats 56 in the Senate, while air traffic chaos drew calls for Sean Duffy's resignation as he sought $50 billion to upgrade the system. Neither falls on the late-October peak, and nothing else in the fortnight's reporting accounts for it.

poly-will-bola-tinubu-win-the-2027-niger.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Bola Tinubu wins Nigeria's 2027 presidential election. Its price is what traders will pay on a second term for the president of Africa's most populous country.
poly-will-bola-tinubu-win-the-2027-niger.recent: The fortnight's Nigerian election news was about the vote's machinery, not the incumbent: Nigeria's electoral commission blamed 54 officials for fake voter records, and in Gombe armed men blocked Isa Pantami's convoy with burning tyres. Neither story accounts for what traders will pay on Tinubu.
